title: Frontier E: integer-structure distinguishers null; generic-model and decision-tree size remarks
question: Frontier E (ECDLP-41), integer structure, all NEGATIVE at p=524309 (two prime-order curves, seeds 1,2): E1 local carry/bit/order/difference correlations x(Q) vs x(Q+jP) null (2% planted signal detected, z 28-760); E2 index differences of integer-sorted neighbours null; E6 three-term carry c_k=[x_{k+1}+x_{k-1}>=p] (amendment hashed before running) fails the pre-registered two-seed rule (p_T=0.025, 0.050 at different h; positive control p_T=0.005); E4 HNP-lattice and E5 lifting-smoothness killed by derivation/literature (E5: ~2^18-bit numerators at rank 29 for 256-bit p). Unreviewed derivations: (E0) ordered/bit access is already free in Shoup generic model so any sub-sqrt(r) algorithm needs a distinguisher of k->x(kP) from a random injection that also leaks k; (E3) with comparisons and free constants, decision-tree arithmetic length is vacuous without tree-size accounting (affects HYP-dbe79a50 interpretation).
rationale: Integer structure is the only resource left unconstrained by the barrier map.
